prompt: What is the canonical churn rate as of 2026-09-30, split by region?
answer_text:
2 row(s).
Groups of fewer than 5 people are never shown (0 left out here).
Assumption: Used the canonical churn_rate definition: customers with no revenue order in the last 90 days (is_churned) divided by customers who have ordered (has_ordered), measured as of 2026-09-30.
Assumption: Region is taken from region_code in rpt_customer_churn.
Assumption: Did not use marketing's legacy 180-day definition (is_churned_marketing).
Documented caveat (cav_as_of_date): "Recency, churn, activity and tenure are measured against the as_of_date var (2026-09-30), the last day of loaded data, not today's date."
Documented caveat (cav_two_churn_definitions): "There are two churn definitions. Customer Insights' churn_rate (canonical) is 90 days without an order, among customers who have ordered. Marketing's churn_rate_marketing is 180 days and counts never-ordered customers as churned. When someone says "churn", ask which one; default to churn_rate."
Tables: rpt_customer_churn

sql: SELECT "rpt_customer_churn"."region_code" AS "region_code", CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN "rpt_customer_churn"."is_churned" THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DECIMAL) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN "rpt_customer_churn"."has_ordered" THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS "churn_rate" FROM "marts"."rpt_customer_churn" AS "rpt_customer_churn" GROUP BY "rpt_customer_churn"."region_code" HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT "rpt_customer_churn"."customer_id") >= 5 ORDER BY "region_code" LIMIT 1001
